source.public_versification_note: Public and Hebrew numbering align throughout Numbers 9–10. All 59 exact original records are hashed, including eight source annotations across 9:3, 9:10, 9:21, 10:9, 10:25, 10:34 and 10:36. Later book numbering differences require separate mapping.

key_decisions.decision: Retain day fourteen, appointed time and both all-statute/all-regulation clauses; twilight matches Exodus 12, with the disputed between-the-evenings idiom noted.
Keep the men as a specific group, corpse-related ritual impurity, inability rather than refusal, and both same-day references; no invented moral fault.
Resolve him as Moses and preserve the men’s question about exclusion from the communal offering; appointed time remains explicit.
Express the distributive anyone and future generations inclusively, retaining both exceptions and distant as written despite its extraordinary dot; permission continues with the alternate date.
Retain both prohibitions and all applicable Passover statutes; it still refers to the sacrifice rather than to an abstract festival.
Preserve both conditions and the severe cut-off sanction, with its reason and bearing sin; generic legal person is inclusive, while the sanction’s unspecified mechanism remains open.
Retain resident status, conditional participation, both legal terms and one shared rule; do not add broader civic claims or silently waive Exodus 12’s conditions.
Keep tabernacle/tent-of-testimony identification and appearance rather than assert ordinary combustion; preserve evening-to-morning duration.
Preserve the continuing pattern without importing the words by day from other witnesses; clarify the nocturnal appearance from verse 15.
Retain the overnight case and read day/night as times of departure, noting the alternative duration reading; bind both source accent and punctuation annotations exactly.
Preserve two days/month/year sequence, interpreting days as year in this extended-duration idiom with alternative noted; keep both the negative and positive movement clauses.
